idiom_name: class/struct with methods and private setters; partial types only to split one declaration physically
implementation_notes: A C# class already groups data and behaviour; the contour discipline is making the members express the concept - domain-named methods instead of public setters - and keeping every part of one type discoverable, with partial types reserved for splitting generated code from hand-written parts of the same declaration. Extension methods do not extend the concept: they see only the public surface, bind statically, and the framework design guidelines say to prefer instance methods on types you own, reserving extensions for interface helper functionality and dependency-avoidance cases.
pitfalls: Extension methods cannot see private state and are resolved statically: a later instance method with the same name silently shadows them, and a concept extended across many static classes becomes undiscoverable.
Public get/set on every property is the anemic-model signature in C#; private setters or domain-named operations keep the contour meaningful.
partial types let one type sprawl across the assembly - all parts must be compiled together and any part can mutate the same fields, so use them for code generation, not as a filing system.
